items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: we had a band, it was composed of Howard Brockington, Big Nick, Thad my brother—No, the bass player was Peynton, Lutellis Peynton. He was the one I told you about earlier. Big Nick was, of course, the leader of the band.

ctx.x: I once talk specifically about early piano influences like Tatum and Heinz. But, since we digress, I don't want to forget about Big Nick Nicholas.

Right, Big, I met him – – we had a band, it was composed of Howard Brockington, Big Nick, Thad my brother—No, the bass player was Peynton, Lutellis Peynton. He was the one I told you about earlier. Big Nick was, of course, the leader of the band. We, actually didn’t work in Grand Rapids. He came down to the Pontiac area. We worked in…let me think…I think we played one job in Grand Rapids because I remember driving from Pontiac in my car, well, in my father’s car. We drove back in a horrible snowstorm all the way…
Was he fully developed at that time? Was that early on like Lucky Thompson?

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: Hank Jones was playin' piano there for a long time

ctx.x: So, when I get off from work I come home from the beach and I would start jammin' in the lounge and I'd start doin' the same thing I was doin' in the Paradise, because I did it for nothin'. Because I just wanted to blow; I didn't want to go to bed. Everybody's in town, Jimmy Durante or Sammy Davis or Louis (Armstrong) or Nat King Cole, Billy Eckstine, everybody was in. And they would all come there, when they got off from work. So I became the M.C. and, you know, and so we created somethin'. So then the manager…

on in there and I worked there another eight weeks. So, in other words, it worked out all right. (laughter) Then Wells, of Wells Chicken Shack, you know, he's been up there (Harlem) for years. He was down (in Florida) on vacation and so Austin Powell and I... Austin and I stayed and we got local fellows to play the rhythm and so Wells says, "Look here, why don't you come up to my place in Harlem?" So when we left down there we went right on up and worked in Wells' Chicken Shack and at different times I had Oscar…
What kind of a program was it? Was it similar at all to the Paradise?
